sampling_model.design: For each fixed even \(m\), one-record laws belong to \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\); the observed experiment is \(\mathbb P_{P,n}=\{P\circ(X,A,L)^{-1}\}^{\otimes n}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent draws from the observed marginal of one fixed-\(m\) full-data law, with only \(X,A,L\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of both potential losses conditional on \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell-arm has known probability \(1/(2m)\); realized counts may be zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All \(2m\) survival tails are estimated from raw random-count samples by a total thresholded Hall procedure; no nuisance convergence rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper estimates a policy maximizing a fixed marginal potential-outcome quantile and derives nonstandard fixed-level asymptotics.

Its one-tail Hall results motivate the coordinatewise benchmark after the translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\). Each conditional tail here is a compact translated slice of that one-tail class, while the full randomized \(2m\)-tail causal experiment is a stricter product construction. The translated coordinatewise benchmark is minimax-equivalent in the familywise phase and the saturated strict sub-familywise phase, but the unsaturated capacity-mixture upper frontier does not follow from their theorems.

Theorem 1 lower-bounds honest scalar tail confidence length by worst-case bias and the paper constructs a bias-aware interval.

body.tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture. The coordinatewise benchmark is minimax-sharp throughout the familywise phase \(A_{n,m,\tau}\ge[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), including saturation. It is also sharp, at order \(\ell\), in the strict sub-familywise region where \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\ge\ell\); every \(N<1\) case satisfying the sub-familywise inequality lies there. Only the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region retains a selected-mixture regret gap. The simultaneous-inference width converse and exact shrinking criterion remain a separate open question.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-level quantile-policy methods do not address extrapolated Hall tails. One-tail Hall theory supplies the translated coordinatewise benchmark, which is proved unavoidable both in the familywise phase and on the saturated strict sub-familywise subset, but neither it nor regular policy-learning theory supplies the capacity-aware oracle inequality needed in the remaining unsaturated region.
project_justification.niche: For each fixed even cell count, randomization identifies every policy mixture and capacity optimization is computable by sorting. Heterogeneous indices, local ties, empty observed cells, and growing mixture mass remain in the model; the paired-splice argument handles unrestricted reallocation and, together with the new saturation corollary, isolates the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region where selected-mixture averaging could improve on familywise estimation.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the generic full-class regret sandwich, the exact two-cell frontier, a multiscale paired-splice lower envelope, and the matched coordinatewise frontier in two regions: the familywise phase and the saturated strict sub-familywise phase. It proves that every \(N<1\) sub-familywise case belongs to the latter and that every vanishing-regret sequence is asymptotically separated from the regular additive-policy benchmark. The only remaining regret problem is the exact upper frontier in the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region; confidence-width optimality remains separate.

body.related_work: CarpentierKim2015 is one-tail statistical substrate, not a capacity-policy theorem. Each conditional tail in this note is a compact translated slice of its one-tail Hall class after the parameter conversion \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), while the full randomized causal experiment couples \(2m\) such tails through a stricter product construction. The present paired-splice converse and coordinatewise upper bound prove equivalence to the translated coordinatewise benchmark in the familywise phase and, by saturation, on a strict sub-familywise subset; in the remaining unsaturated region, CarpentierKim2015 supplies no selected-mixture oracle inequality. A paired-splice converse transfers upward only to an explicitly defined superclass containing every constructed full-data law; an upper bound must be rechecked on that superclass and does not transfer from the splice. AtheyWager2021 and KitagawaTetenov2018 concern regular additive welfare, and the proved implication \(\mathcal R/\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}\to\infty\) on every vanishing-regret sequence shows that their \(\sqrt{m/n}\)-type scale is not the extreme-tail frontier. WangZhouSongSherwood2018 and XiaZhangKong2026 occupy fixed-level quantile-policy identification or learning. OsamaZachariahStoica2020 supplies the non-nested marginal upper-cost-quantile consumer objective; it is neither a class-inclusion statement nor a rate engine for this Hall experiment. Its support-based conformal limit motivates the extrapolation question but does not establish the answer. Predetermined heterogeneous-tail pooling, scalar tail intervals, and fixed-pair extreme-treatment inference likewise do not resolve selection among capacity-constrained mixtures.
body.interpretation: The phase map now has two certified regions. At or above the familywise elbow \(A_{n,m,\tau}=[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), rare cellwise errors make coordinatewise calibration minimax-unavoidable. Below the elbow, if the multiscale selected-mixture term \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\) reaches \(\ell\), the logarithmic regret saturates and the coordinatewise benchmark is again sharp; this automatically covers every \(N<1\) case that is sub-familywise. Only when both inequalities are strict can capacity averaging possibly improve the coordinatewise rate.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The distributional lower-side obstruction is resolved. Comparison with the coordinatewise upper theorem closes the familywise phase, and direct use of the lower envelope closes the saturated strict sub-familywise phase at \(\mathcal R\asymp_{\beta,D}\ell\asymp\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}\). The residual regret step is confined to \(A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa}\) and \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]<\ell\): no proved learner controls data-dependent selected tail weights at the lower rate without reverting to the coordinatewise maximum. Thus \(A_{n,m,\tau}\to0\) is proved necessary and \(A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\to0\) sufficient for vanishing regret, but equality of these criteria remains open only inside that last region. The confidence-width converse and exact shrinking condition remain separately open.
body.honest_scope: Established claims are the fixed-cell Hall model and identification setup, sorting and inversion, Hall-core approximation, the local-dominance map, the generic coordinatewise regret sandwich, the exact two-cell rate, the simultaneous confidence upper system, the multiscale paired-splice lower envelope, the matched familywise regret frontier, and the saturated strict sub-familywise frontier. The lower envelope is not described as the exact frontier in the remaining unsaturated region. The exact unsaturated capacity-aware upper rate and the sharp confidence-width frontier remain open. No common tail index, fixed gap, density, nonempty realized cell sample, nuisance-rate assumption, or selection penalty is imposed. A paired-splice converse may be exported only to a superclass explicitly containing its full-data laws; the corresponding upper bound requires a separate proof.
